The result of the Road Race held on the 6th inst. at Wimbledon was a very popular one and but for the fact that the first five men found more than " the bit " extra, it would have been a very close handicap indeed, at any rate it was a very interesting race to witness and when our old friend G.

G Tyrer, a veteran, who was second last year in the corresponding race, was limit man, and went off at his usual jog-trot. He was overhauled, however, after covering about a mile, Canard passing him in company with Colman and Strange S.
However, that old stalwart George Still and veteran George Tyrer both did their bit, and we came out on top, winners by a fair margin of points
Still (who incidentally won a Club 7 in 1908, but not being first-claim at the time, did not qualify for the Championship Medal), H. Goodfellow and G.
The race was a handicap of the kind in which everyone does the same distance, and in which time starts are given The first man off was the veteran, G.

As already stated, five runners beat fifteen minutes, and no less than nine others beat sixteen minutes, scratch time, and only seven men took more than 17 minutes, scratch time. As usual in this handicap the veteran G. Tyrer went off first, but this year he was off form and was caught fairly quickly.
Our old friend, George Tyrer, was away first at a nice, steady pace. Seven minutes later Arthur Penny started in pursuit of a large field of runners, looking as if he meant to catch them all.

George Tyrer was first man away, followed by the other 30 odd runners at intervals of a few seconds, with Arthur Penny as scratch man. George Tyrer held the lead for some time but had to give way to youth before the end.
As to the race itself: George Tyrer went off with his usual long start, with George Still going off next, and George managed to keep in front until nearing home.

George Tyrer, one of our oldest members, and who nowadays turns up about once a year, missed the A.G.M., but came along the following week, looking not much different, but perhaps a few years older, otherwise just the same jolly old self.

John Rowland never fails to visit us when on vacation from his medical studies at Aberdeen, where he has revived interest in running amongst his fellow students. George Tyrer has been unable to visit us as he has been working seven days a week. Perhaps we will be seeing him next season.
George Tyrer, our oldest cross-country runner, looked in at the Hall recently. Syd King has been out training again; it looks as if we are going to see some old faces in our post-war teams.

Another old-timer in George Tyrer was present but only as an on-looker. When they came in sight of the finish our old friend Bert Mitchell was in the lead followed by young Dick Savage, with a new youngster in E.

Those of you who have not yet paid your subscriptions might be interested to know that one of the first subs. to be received was from 78 years old G.TYRER, who said in his accompanying letter,"...so when you no longer continue to get my sub. you will know I have buzzed off"!!
We also have to announce the death of another old stalwart, George Tyrer, known to several generations of members as the man who made a point of turning out in the September road-run every year.
G.
